audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows contradicted the content layer's own whys: Level 1 was credited to Lillia when the text says 'He owns level 1 outright', and Levels 3, 4-5, First item and 2+ items were credited to Renekton when the text calls them her takeover, her peak, and 'it only gets worse for him'.
audit.why: Renekton's entire threat is a 300-range point-and-click stun on a full Fury bar in the first two levels. Once Blooming Blows is stacking Move Speed and Swirlseed is up, a champion whose longest reach is a 450 dash cannot start a trade, and he has no sustain outside Cull the Meek's small heal.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Renekton / Skill / Lillia / Lillia / Lillia / Lillia / Lillia with ratings 3, 5, 7, 8, 7, 7, 7 as matched full+content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rated TRICKY, difficulty 7/10 with a 7.5/10 carry threat, against a 90% win rate and a chart that belongs to Lillia from level 3 onward.
audit.why: Both the data and the page's own prose say this is a favoured lane once the first two levels are survived.
audit.corrected: Difficulty lowered to 4/10, carry threat 5/10, and the rating strings rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer twice calls Cull the Meek his gap-closer ('his Q closes distance', 'every time he dashes in with Q'), and the packet notes no Renekton ability is ever named on the page.
audit.why: Cull the Meek is a 325-range AoE swing that heals him; the dash is Slice and Dice (E, 450 range, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s). Ruthless Predator is 300 range and stuns 0.75s, or 1.5s and shield-destroying above 50 Fury. Knowing the stun is 300 range is what makes 'farm at the outer edge of Q' actionable rather than vague.
audit.corrected: The dash reattributed to Slice and Dice, and the real names and ranges written into the level-chart whys.

audit.why: The itemization line already says to add anti-heal early into his sustain, which is right: Cull the Meek heals more above 50 Fury and is the only healing in his kit.

notes: The content prose here is good and the chart was simply inverted against it — five of seven rows said Renekton wins stages the same file describes as Lillia's takeover, on a 90% win rate. Cull the Meek was twice called his gap-closer; the dash is Slice and Dice.
